html:
The Urarina, who call themselves Kacha Edze, are an Indigenous people of the Peruvian Amazon. They live along the Chambira River and other streams in the lowlands of Loreto. Their language is an isolate, unrelated to any other known language.

They live in small villages by the rivers, fish, hunt and grow manioc and plantains. Their neighbours include the Kandozi and the Shiwilu. Jesuit missions touched the area in the 1600s, and the rubber boom of the late 1800s brought forced labour. Later came oil drilling, which has polluted some of their rivers in Peru. A few thousand Urarina live there today.
